text.p: September notionnel futures traded on MATIF will remain firmly in their bullish trend on Wednesday but see some consolidation before pushing higher, technical analysts said.

"The way we've seen the market move since the low of July 1 at 129.02 has been a progressive step for notionnel," said Anil Patel, technical analyst at Nomura International in London. "We've seen six consecutive days of higher highs and higher lows so we are really in a trend here."
Patel said any pull backs within the bullish market would meet support at the recent lows of 130.30, 129.96 and 129.80.
At 0818 GMT, September notionnel futures were at 130.70, up 32 basis points.
Brenda Sullivan, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said notionnel looked well supported with a good upward trend for the near term.
"But for now momentum is looking overdone. The daily RSI came off bit from the 80 value, suggesting we might see a bit of a retreat towards 130.12, a minor retracement level," she said.
Sullivan said a correction was also due as the contract had completed a full Elliott wave to the upside when it moved up to test a wave extension target of 130.58.
"If we can get down through 130.12 then we are likely to see 129.80 this week," she said. "We have to hold support there, or at most at 129.54, then look for it to go up again."
To the upside, Sullivan said resistance was at 130.88 and then 131.24, the high for June on the continuation chart.
Patel said the initial upside level to break was 130.76, the high on May 16 on the continuation chart. Above there he noted 130.92, the low on March 12.
"The (March 12) close at 131.06 is a key point to close above and if we do then we could be heading towards 131.50," he said.
At the short end September Pibor was at 96.59, down 0.01 on the day.
